question: Is Toxocara seropositivity associated with eosinophilia?
refined_question: Among noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2011-2012 (Age >=18 years), is toxocara seropositivity - IgG antibody positive (Luminex rTc-CTL-1, MFI >23.1) associated with a higher prevalence of eosinophilia - absolute eosinophil count >=0.5 x10^9/L, after adjustment for age, sex, race and ethnicity, income-to-poverty ratio, body mass index, and born in the united states?
title: Association of Toxocara Seropositivity With Eosinophilia Among US Adults: NHANES 2011-2012
hypothesis: Toxocara seropositivity - IgG antibody positive (Luminex rTc-CTL-1, MFI >23.1) is associated with a higher prevalence of eosinophilia - absolute eosinophil count >=0.5 x10^9/L.

pico.population: noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2011-2012 (Age >=18 years)
pico.exposure: Toxocara seropositivity - IgG antibody positive (Luminex rTc-CTL-1, MFI >23.1)
pico.covariates: Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, and Born in the United States

exposure.label: Toxocara seropositivity - IgG antibody positive (Luminex rTc-CTL-1, MFI >23.1)

model.rationale: Binary outcome: survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression with log link estimates prevalence ratios (PRs). PRs are preferred to odds ratios for cross-sectional data because ORs exaggerate associations when the outcome is common (>10%); the quasi-Poisson variance is robust under the design-based (Taylor linearization) estimator. Logistic regression is run as a sensitivity analysis.

adjustment_sets.label: Adjusted for age, sex, and race and ethnicity

missing_data.rationale: Complete-case primary analysis within the design; multiple imputation by chained equations as sensitivity analysis when covariates are missing.

rationale.statistician: Binary outcome: survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression with log link estimates prevalence ratios (PRs). PRs are preferred to odds ratios for cross-sectional data because ORs exaggerate associations when the outcome is common (>10%); the quasi-Poisson variance is robust under the design-based (Taylor linearization) estimator. Logistic regression is run as a sensitivity analysis.
rationale.epidemiologist: Covariates were selected as plausible common causes of toxocara seropositivity - IgG antibody positive (Luminex rTc-CTL-1, MFI >23.1) and eosinophilia - absolute eosinophil count >=0.5 x10^9/L (minimal confounder set from the domain library): Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, and Born in the United States. Variables on the causal pathway or sharing laboratory components with the outcome/exposure are excluded to avoid over-adjustment.

limitations: Cross-sectional design: temporality cannot be established and associations must not be interpreted causally.
Single measurement of laboratory values; within-person variability and chronicity cannot be assessed.
Residual confounding by unmeasured or imperfectly measured factors (e.g., diet, medications, menstrual blood loss).
Self-reported comorbidities and behaviours are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.
NHANES excludes institutionalized and active-duty military populations.
Operational definition (Toxocara IgG+): Surplus-specimen subsample (participants aged 6+ with stored sera): analysed with the surplus-specimen weights (WTSSTT2Y), not the full exam weights.
Operational definition (Toxocara IgG+): Seropositivity reflects past or current exposure, not active larval infection.
Operational definition (Toxocara IgG+): 2013-2014 results exist but the current CDC release does not include their subsample weights; 2011-2012 is used.
